[C11] Council bans late bicycle bells. The Kalderwick council voted 9 to 4 to forbid bicycle bells between midnight and five in the morning under ordinance 22-B. Supporters cited complaints from residents of Lowmarch Heights, where narrow streets carry the sound of every passing rider into bedroom windows. The cyclists' group Spokewise called the measure a nuisance that will not improve sleep, and argued that a gentle bell is safer than a shout when riders approach pedestrians in the dark. The ordinance takes effect at the start of next month, with a warning period of thirty days before fines of 15 thaler are issued.

[C12] Lumen Footbridge opens. Mayor Odalys Brenthorne-Vale cut the ribbon on the Lumen Footbridge, a glass-floored span costing 18.2 million thaler that links the old market quarter with the new riverside park. The Kalderwick Gazette reported that the bridge glows amber after dusk and carries about 6,000 walkers a day. Engineers tested the deck with a convoy of loaded carts before the opening, and the mayor admitted in her speech that she had avoided looking down while crossing. Critics noted that the project ran eleven months late, but visitors praised the view of the estuary at sunset.

[C13] Glass fog halts ferries. A rare glass fog, a dense freezing mist, reduced visibility to twelve metres across the Kalderwick estuary on Tuesday. Harbour ferries were cancelled for six hours and commuters were redirected to trams and to a temporary bus service along the embankment. Meteorologists said the fog formed when warm air from the south slid over water that had cooled overnight, coating railings and rigging with a thin film of ice. Schools opened an hour late, and two flights were delayed. The weather office advised residents to expect a repeat on Wednesday morning, though it predicted the mist would lift earlier.

[C14] Bakery wins Golden Crumb. Fennimore & Daughters took the annual Golden Crumb prize for its saffron-rye twist. Judge Aurelio Pennywhistle praised the crust and the faint smoke flavour, calling it the most original loaf he had tasted in his eleven years on the panel. The bakery sold out within two hours of the announcement, and a queue stretched along Cobbler Street until mid-afternoon. Owner Marguerite Fennimore said the recipe came from her grandmother, who baked in a wood oven behind the family shop. The runner-up was a honey-barley cob from a village bakery in the hills, and third place went to a plum-seed roll.

[C15] Tram line 7 extension. Tram line 7 has been extended to Lowmarch Heights with fourteen new stops. Journey times from the central station fall from 38 to 29 minutes, and the transport office expects daily ridership on the line to rise by a third. The scheduler that plans the new timetable is still being tuned by the transport office, which has asked riders to report crowded services through its website. Trams now run every seven minutes at peak hours and every fifteen minutes after nine in the evening. The extension required relaying two kilometres of track and moving a gas main, and it was completed under budget.
